tagline: SR 16 along an old trading path from Eatonton to Sparta.
intro: The corridor plan's main leg follows SR 16 east from western Putnam County through the Oconee National Forest to Eatonton's courthouse square and the Oconee River. In Hancock County it crosses Shoulderbone Creek and runs through Sparta to Jewell at the Warren County line, where a separate extension carries SR 16 on to Warrenton. A loop north of Sparta and county roads toward Linton make up the rest of the 82 miles.

The plan traces SR 16 to the Okfuskee Path, where Native traders carried deer pelts and settlers from Virginia and the Carolinas later came. Dairying followed in 1876, when Benjamin Hunt brought fifteen cows to Putnam County, and Eatonton is now known as the Dairy Capital of Georgia.

moments.title: Rock Hawk
moments.text: Off SR 16 on Wallace Dam Road lies a quartzite bird thought to be the work of Woodland people, though it now takes some imagination to see a bird, let alone a hawk.

moments.title: Shoulderbone Creek
moments.text: The corridor plan describes an early 20th-century bridge here with the Millmore gristmill in view, on the creek that gave its name to the 1786 treaty ceding Creek lands east of the Oconee.

moments.title: Sparta
moments.text: Sherman's march left Sparta entirely unscathed in 1864, reportedly because a Confederate captain, son-in-law to a local industrialist, steered the Union troops elsewhere.
